title: Private Deploy Console - network & KMS onboarding grooming
content:
Purpose:
Quick grooming + wireframe notes for the Private Deploy Admin Console onboarding flow focused on networking (VPC, subnets, routing, peering/transit) and key material integrations (KMS/HSM). This doc collects UX decisions, validation rules, edge cases, and acceptance criteria for MVP and stretch items.

Audience:
- Product PMs (private-deploy)
- Console UX/UI engineers
- Solutions engineers/professional services (for field validation needs)
- Infra/SRE for preflight checks and networking constraints

High-level goals:
- Make it safe and predictable for infra teams to connect Redwood Private control plane to their network and key management provider
- Surface minimal required info up front and hide advanced options behind an "Advanced network" drawer
- Provide deterministic preflight checks (connectivity, firewall, DNS, IAM/KMS permissions) with actionable remediation suggestions
- Support multi-region deployments with clear defaults and region mapping UI

MVP scope (must-have):
- Stepper-based onboarding: 1) Basic info + region selection, 2) VPC & subnets, 3) Routing & egress, 4) KMS selection + key details, 5) Review & run preflight, 6) Launch (or schedule).
- UI for selecting existing VPC (AWS/GCP/Azure) or choosing to let Redwood provision an isolated VPC (for private on-prem option, this mode is a placeholder).
- Ability to specify per-region subnet CIDR(s) and whether each subnet is public/private; validation to detect overlapping CIDRs across regions/tenants.

(continued) Networking details and UX notes:
- Primary panel: region dropdown with chips for selected regions. On selection, expand region card to collect region-specific networking: VPC id, availability zones, subnets, route table ids, and a checkbox: "Bring your own VPC (BYOVPC)" vs "Redwood-managed VPC".
- If BYOVPC: require at least one private subnet for inference traffic and an optional public subnet for management egress. Inline help text: "Private subnets must allow outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints (see preflight step)."
- Subnet discovery: allow user to paste a VPC id and click "fetch subnets" (call to backend returns list). UX fallback: manual entry fields for CIDR and AZ if discovery fails. Indicate permissions error (403) if role/account lacks Describe permissions.
- Routing: optional fields for custom route targets (NAT Gateway, Transit Gateway, InternetGateway). Checkbox: "Use customer-managed NAT / TGW". If selected, show fields for peering or TGW attachment id.
- Egress IP / Static egress: small input if customers require whitelisting; show recommended steps for each cloud (AWS: NAT elastic IP; GCP: Cloud NAT with static IP; Azure: NAT Gateway).
- Cross-account peering: special row with short copy: "Supports cross-account VPC peering for AWS. Provide peer account id and role ARN for automatic peering create (requires permissions)." Include link to Solutions Engineer runbook.
- Networking validation checklist (run in preflight):
  - Control plane reachability on ports 443 and 5222 (for service-to-service)
  - DNS resolution for control-plane hostnames (support for split-horizon DNS notes)
  - Route table entries to allow outbound to Redwood egress IPs (or proxy)
  - NAT/Firewall allowlist for health checks + kernel-level metadata calls
  - Subnet size >= /27 recommended for provisioning pods and buffer
- Failure states and UX: if preflight fails, show grouped errors by severity (blocking / warning / info) with copy + suggested commands (aws cli, gcloud) and a "Request help from SRE" quick-link that opens a support ticket prepopulated with diagnostic bundle.

KMS/HSM notes (UX + integration):
- Offer three modes in KMS step: 1) Redwood-managed keys (fastest), 2) Customer-managed KMS (cloud KMS), 3) Customer HSM (bring-your-own HSM or HSM cluster).
- Selection card layout: small icons and a short 1-line risk/cost blurb (example: "Customer-managed KMS: you retain key ownership, Redwood needs Encrypt/Decrypt and IAM policies to use keys for model encryption and audit logging.").
- KMS details to collect when customer-managed KMS selected: provider (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault), key ARN / resource id, key policy role ARN or service principal. 
- For HSM: require certificate PEM upload + attestation token (if using vendor-managed HSM) or instructions to open a TLS tunnel to customer HSM endpoint. Show example curl for HSM health check.
- Key import & rotation UI: show current key fingerprint, created/rotation schedule, and a "Rotate key" button that triggers a staged rotation with verification window. For HSM, rotation is a manual step with operator guidance.
- Validation checks for keys: list of checks in preflight
  - Key accessible via provided role/principal (attempt a symmetric encrypt/decrypt of a test blob)
  - Key policy allows Redwood service principal to Encrypt/Decrypt and CreateGrant (if needed)
  - HSM attestation verifies certificate chain; if using PKCS#11, ensure connector responds to list slots call.
- UX failure examples: show copy for "permission denied on key" with one-click helper that generates a sample policy snippet for AWS/GCP/Azure.

Wireframe elements / microcopy suggestions:
- Stepper top-left with progress label: "Region 1 of N" and small secondary line: "Network details required for each selected region."
- Right-side contextual panel that surfaces the preflight summary (green/yellow/red dots) and active blockers; this panel persists across steps.
- Inline "Why do we need this?" toggles that expand brief technical rationale and link to long-form docs (Confluence).
- Error banner examples: "Preflight failed: missing route to control-plane. Action: add route to 10.20.30.0/24 -> nat-xxxxx or contact SRE. [Open runbook] [Request help]"
- Small copy for KMS card footnote: "We only store key references. Encryption of model artifacts happens using a per-tenant envelope key. Bring-your-own-HSM requires additional attestation steps."

Backlog / grooming items (priority ordered):
- P0: Implement preflight engine endpoints (SRE/infra) + front-end hook to run preflight and render structured results.
- P0: Basic stepper + per-region cards + VPC discovery flow (auto-populate subnets).
- P1: KMS selection cards + policy-generator snippets for AWS/GCP/Azure.
- P1: Error helper flows that open support ticket + attach diagnostics.
- P2: Cross-account peering automation for AWS (service role flow); requires infra support for auto-peering with safeguards.
- P3: HSM connector flow (TLS tunnel + attestation wizard) - research only for Q3.
- P3: Support for IPv6 subnets (defer to later; note compatibility issues).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Customer can complete the UI flow and submit a configuration for one region where:
  - At least one private subnet with valid CIDR is specified
  - KMS mode is selected (Redwood-managed or customer KMS)
  - Preflight runs and returns a pass or lists actionable blocking issues
- Console shows clear remediation text and links for all blocking preflight errors
- On success, a config object (API payload) is generated and visible in review step matching shape in linked Confluence doc
- Support ticket + diagnostic bundle can be triggered from the failed preflight UI with a single click

Unresolved questions / open decisions:
- Should we allow saving a partial onboarding state (for multi-region setups where infra teams complete region-by-region)? Prefer yes, but need API support for draft configs.
- How much automation for cross-account peering should we provide vs just instructions and a template? (security review required)
- HSM UX: do we support vendor connectors directly in MVP or just a documented manual process? (Tentatively manual)
- RBAC: who gets to see the KMS key ARNs in the console? Add mask/permission to hide sensitive identifiers?

Notes for implementation teams:
- Frontend: build stepper and contextual right rail as reusable components; preflight API returns array of {id, severity, message, remediationLinks[], rawLogsUrl}. Render severity grouping and enable expand/collapse.
- Backend: preflight should be idempotent and cache results for 10 minutes; capture trace id for support bundles.
- SRE: define hardened list of egress IPs and healthcheck endpoints; provide Terraform module for TGW/TGW attachments for internal tests.
- Solutions Eng: draft policy snippets for AWS KMS, GCP KMS IAM roles, and Azure Key Vault RBAC and publish to Confluence.

Quick copy snippets for UI (poppable tooltips):
- "Private subnet": "Used for hosting inference workloads. Must have outbound connectivity to the Redwood control plane."
- "Preflight": "Run connectivity and permission checks to verify the configuration before provisioning. Fix blockers or request help."
- "Customer-managed KMS": "You control the key. Redwood will request limited permissions to use this key for encrypting tenant material."

Next steps / meeting plan:
- Sync with SRE on preflight API contract (JIRA-PD-4212) — 2026-03-12 lead: Liam
- UX critique of wireframes in Figma — 2026-03-05 lead: Aisha
- Solutions Eng to finalize policy snippets — 2026-03-18 lead: Marisol
- Decide on draft-save behavior by 2026-03-22 (dependent on API)

TODO (short list):
- [ ] Add sample API payloads to linked Confluence doc (owner: Dev)
- [ ] Add support-runbook link text into UI help panel (owner: SRE)
- [ ] Prototype subnet discovery error states (frontend)

Notes-to-self: when writing copy, avoid heavy jargon in the onboarding flow; show advanced terms behind links. If the customer selects HSM, surface a clear "contact PS" CTA early — that flow will be manual for MVP.

Reviewers: please comment inline on the Figma file for microcopy and on the Confluence doc for API shape.

End of doc.
